newsitem.title: GERMANY: Softer dollar continues to hit German shares.
newsitem.headline: Softer dollar continues to hit German shares.

text.p: The softer U.S. dollar plagued sentiment on the German stock exchange on Wednesday, rendering the prospect of significant new gains on the IBIS DAX index increasingly unlikely as the day wore on.
Dealers had been looking to Wall Street to provide the kind of inspiration it had given the market on Tuesday, when it rose lifting German shares in its wake.
But U.S. stocks opened lower and by 1428 GMT the IBIS DAX index was mired at lower levels at 3,338.70 points, down 30.56 points or 0.91 percent, with June DAX DTB futures down 24.5 points at 3,348.5.
"We've seen a break because of the lower dollar and we are covering a bit at the moment, but the market is defying logic today," a Frankfurt trader said.
The main feature of the day on the corporate front was German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG which had its annual news conference earlier.

Daimler ended bourse trade strongly ahead after it said that its first quarter 1997 sales rose strongly and predicted profits could grow strongly by the turn of the century as its restructuring plan takes hold.
The shares ended bourse up 1.25 marks at 138.15 marks.
But in post-bourse trade Daimler shares were lower, down 3.80 marks at 135.50 marks, a fall of 2.73 percent.
"Daimler didn't really excite initially. Their figures are in U.S. GAAP, while most people still think in terms of DVFA, and there are taxes to be taken into account," a trader said.
Dealers were waiting to see the result of its analysts' meeting this afternoon.
Porsche was up 90 marks at 2,200 marks, boosted by an upgrade by Lehman Brothers earlier in the day and among the top performers on Wednesday.
